Subject: Post-call recap & suggested side-by-side tests

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Helpful to hear where Atlas Retail is prioritizing inference: product search ranking, personalized merchandising, and a smaller number of high-throughput chat experiences for store staff. As promised, I wanted to summarize the competitive differences we discussed and propose a focused test plan so you can evaluate parity vs the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Key differentiators we discussed (short version):
- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked streaming with low tail latency and keeps connection state for interruptions (useful for long responses and teleprompts).
- Tool/function calling: First-class structured tool invocation + deterministic tooling contracts; we surface call traces in Console for debugging.
- Structured outputs: Schema enforcement with post-parse validation and automatic rerun hints when validation fails.
- Cost controls: Intelligent batching + prefix KV caching that reduces per-token cost for repeat queries (relevant to your high-reuse queries).
- Reliability: Smart routing and graceful fallback to compatible quantized variants during capacity pressure.

Proposed side-by-side test plan (concrete, 3-day lab):
1) Streaming latency probe (day 1): 1k requests, simulated store workflows. Measure first-byte latency and tail (95/99). Compare to hyperscaler live endpoint.
2) Function/tool calling fidelity (day 2): Run 200 scripted tool invocations (inventory lookup, price calculation). Confirm tool contract adherence and compare failure rates and observability (traces + logs).
3) Structured output enforcement (day 3): Send 500 prompt variations that should return strictly-shaped JSON. Track schema violations and auto-repair suggestions.

Deliverables from our side: short delta brief (attached), the XLS test plan (attached), a recording of today’s demo (attached), and a lightweight dashboard template showing the metrics we believe matter.

Can you confirm: 1) the stakeholder list we should include (ops + procurement), 2) a preferred 3-day window next week (we suggested Oct 26–28), and 3) whether we should run tests in your eu or us region?

Next steps I propose on our side once you confirm:
- Redwood will spin up a private test harness and share API keys valid for the window.
- Lauren will own the instrumentation and dashboards.
- Aditya will set up the function-calling fixtures and quantized variant for throughput runs.

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation and will block tentative times.

Best,
